input.quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
input.rationale: I read the entire Agreement (all 75 paragraphs of the single operative section) and ran targeted searches for audit, inspection, verification, records and compliance-review language. Kubient has no audit, inspection or usage-verification right against AP anywhere: the Fees and Payment clause (p0023) is a revenue-share under which Kubient contracts with Advertisers, collects and remits to AP within seven days, so there is no AP self-reporting to be audited and no AP underpayment exposure; the Use of Service clause (p0025) imposes compliance covenants but no verification or system-access right; and the only access language (p0001) is AP's general cooperation undertaking to enable delivery of the Services, not an audit or inspection right, and confers no right to enter AP premises or access AP systems. With no audit right binding AP, there is nothing to limit as to frequency, notice, auditor independence, cost allocation or system access, and AP's position is better than the preferred position (which would still permit an annual audit). The absence benefits us, so no redline is proposed. Note for the record only: if Kubient later seeks a usage- or revenue-verification right (for example in an Exhibit), the preferred parameters — once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, off-site where possible, Kubient's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to AP systems — should be inserted at that time.
